newsitem.title: USA: Waste Tech says Harris Waste drops lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Waste Tech says Harris Waste drops lawsuit.

text.p: Waste Technology Corp said Friday that Harris Waste Management Inc dropped its legal action for an injunction against Waste Tech's alleged use of trade secrets by Waste Tech's International Press and Shear Division.

Waste Tech said Harris' action, commenced in 1995, sought to prevent three former Harris employees from continuing as officers at International Press because they were allegedly violating non-compete agreements and using trade secrets allegedly stolen from Harris.

Waste Tech said two Minnesota judges in the Second Judicial District Court in Minneapolis determined that Harris had produced insufficient evidence to establish its claim of a violation of a non-compete agreement.
In an order issued by the court, Waste Tech said Harris has agreed to compensate Waste Tech for certain legal fees and expenses incurred as a result of Harris' lawsuit.

In addition, the order also permits the three International Press officers to apply for sanctions against Harris for bringing the action. Waste Tech said the officers will move promptly for the imposition of such sanctions.

President Ted Flood of Waste Tech said "The sole purpose of (Harris') original action was to impair IPS's (Interational Press's) ability to do business in its market, in which it is in direct competition with Harris."
Flood concluded that now, "we plan to redouble our efforts to increase our market share in the growing waste-handling and recycling markets at home and abroad."
